newsitem.title: UK: UK Treasury Minister Willetts may make statement.
newsitem.headline: UK Treasury Minister Willetts may make statement.

text.p: Junior Treasury Minister David Willetts may make a statement to parliament at 1530 gmt on his future, government sources said on Wednesday.
They said Willetts, Paymaster General, will receive a report by the House of Commons Privileges Committee on his conduct when a government whip, or business manager, at 1330 gmt.
He will be able to study the report before considering whether to ask speaker Betty Boothroyd for permission to make a personal statement, an aide in Prime Minister John Major's office said.

Willetts is alleged to have tried improperly to influence a parliamentary probe into sleaze by advising the chairman of the Privileges Committee, Sir Geoffrey Johnson Smith, how to handle the case of Conservative MP Neil Hamilton.
Hamilton is alleged to have accepted cash from Mohammed Al-Fayed to ask parliamentary questions on his behalf.

Asked what the government felt about Willetts' position, the aide said it was too early to say. "Most of us are waiting to look at the report before coming to any judgements," he said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
